content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text compares the challenger's seed/loins chain and the defender's chain in deciding D6 vs C1, so it is doing the chain-against-chain assessment that K-C governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.","rule_words":"the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires","room":"\"that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires\" — one reading forbids rejecting a footed chain for lack of explicit naming; the other allows noting lack of explicit naming as a support/footing deficiency.","why":"The judge treats the challenger's footed chain as deficient for not explicitly naming Joseph, which is a word-for-word/stating-verse test K-C forbids in chain-against-chain collisions."}
